key_insight: Coordinated, location-specific smart-inverter commands can overload targeted grid corridors at lower DER penetration than uniform fleet commands.
engineering_relevance: Securing DER coordination platforms requires assessing network topology and inverter active/reactive-power control, not just aggregate DER penetration.
method: Optimize location-specific DER active/reactive-power setpoints to maximize loading on a selected corridor.
Compare COBA with four uniform commands: all-off, all-on, maximum reactive absorption, and maximum reactive injection.
Verify resulting grid conditions using MATPOWER power flow.
evidence_signal: On the Hawaii Synthetic Grid-37 Buses case with DER aggregated at 20 selected 69-kV buses, COBA overloaded B86 near 30% penetration and B51 near 55%, while uniform commands produced lower same-target loading.
watch_item: Reported thresholds depend on the synthetic network, inverter capabilities, and single-reference-bus balancing convention; they are not universal grid limits.
paper_title: From Caveman to COBA: Coordinated Optimization-Based Attacks on Grid-Edge Smart Inverters in DER-Rich Power Systems
